body: Did you try clicking in the viewport so it has the focus and then using the keys?

Confirmed. OrbitControls are not responsive to keys if a domElement is passed to the controls constructor.

```
var controls = new THREE.OrbitControls( camera, renderer.domElement );
```

three.js r.65
And by the way, another `window.addEventListener('keydown', function(event)` did not work anymore either. Indeed there seems to be a focus (?) problem.

Confirmed, when replacing: 

```
this.domElement.addEventListener( 'keydown', onKeyDown, false );
```

with 

```
window.addEventListener( 'keydown', onKeyDown, false );
```

we can pass the `renderer.domElement` and the keys work as expected.
No, @q2apro is right : OrbitControls register its keydown event on `window`, not on DOMElement passed in its contructor.
The issue still alive , I removed renderer.domElement and now is working

issue.title: OrbitControls: Add keydown event listener to domElement instead of window.

body:
Still an issue: up/down/left/right keys still don't do anything. And passing the domElement is no longer optional; if I omit it, I get "THREE.OrbitControls: The second parameter "domElement" is now mandatory." and nothing works.

echteinfachtv's workaround from Jan 24, 2014 (setting this.onKeyDown = function and then calling it from an eventListener on the window) still works.

Since `r125` you have to add this line to enable key events:
```js
controls.listenToKeyEvents( window );
```

@Mugen87 What's the current state of this issue? Using Typescript, I get a type error for
```typescript
controls.listenToKeyEvents(window)
```
saying:
```
Argument of type 'Window & typeof globalThis' is not assignable to parameter of type 'HTMLElement'.
```
Right now, keys are not working for `OrbitControls`.
